problem: Production lines combine hardware and software from many vendors with poor unified control.
business_model: Software platform for factories (a manufacturing operating system), pricing not found

founders.name: Soham Sankaran
prior_employers: Cornell University (PhD student, distributed systems and robotics)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. A profile page gives Pashi tenure as January 2020 to December 2020 then advisor to July 2021; he later founded PopVax.

technical_complexity.rationale: Interfacing with all hardware and software on a line means many industrial protocols and real-time control, hard for a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration into production lines would lock customers in if achieved, but nothing shows it was.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes incumbent action against Pashi.

market_need_then: Factories use fragmented control software; no Pashi-specific demand evidence was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand material found beyond YC and aggregator listings.

outcome_analysis: Pashi was a three person YC W20 company building software to operate production lines, led by a single technical founder who left the CTO role within about a year. It is listed Inactive with no public post-mortem or acquisition, so the cause is not public. Funding appears limited to a 500 thousand dollar convertible note per one aggregator.
notes: pashi.com returned 404. The 500K convertible note rests on CB Insights alone and is labeled other because the stage is not a priced round; date unknown. The Pashi tenure dates come from a profile aggregator seen in search results only. Founding year conflict: CB Insights says 2017, YC says 2020. No dated competitor sources were found for the window; First Resonance and others surfaced only from 2021.
